sources.text: Plotter, modem and specialist profiles and drivers require design and qualification. Discovery metadata alone does not guarantee operation.
DRI leads software interfaces; Logix contributes hardware specifications; independent manufacturers participate. Final charter, fees and support period remain open.
Power contacts/current limits and keyed connector pinout require an electrical drawing. Disk/printer devices self-powered; keyboard power is current-limited.
Attach or detach only while the port is quiescent. Ground-first/power sequencing must be defined; no unrestricted live hot-plug claim.
CRC-16-CCITT, polynomial 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, xorout 0x0000; cover unescaped header and payload. Byte order must be frozen in wire specification.
One outstanding request per device initially; explicit ACK/NAK, bounded timeout/retry, device BUSY and response credit.
Sequence/request IDs reject duplicate execution; keep the last completed request/response until session reset.
Reset changes the session epoch. Do not silently retry an unresolved non-idempotent operation such as print output after reset; report uncertain completion to the caller.
500 kbit/s with 8N1 permits at most 50 KB/s before headers, escaping and turnaround; 125 kbit/s permits at most 12.5 KB/s. Keyboard polling must not monopolize CPU during disk transfers.

Use architecture-neutral device descriptors and class protocols. Host OS provides Z80 or ERA class drivers. Optional device-specific ROM drivers must carry explicit ISA/ABI tags; never execute a Z80 ROM driver as ERA code.

Baseline monitors accept vertical-retrace palette commands. From NCC June 1982, explicitly capable Color Pro monitors also accept bounded horizontal-retrace commands under technology.scanline_palette_list; do not send these to legacy monitors.
Host firmware performs selection using controller control-channel registers; monitor fixed capability ROM/straps and serializer.
Use an explicitly configured profile or documented common safe raster; otherwise remain blank. Never infer 640-pixel support from connection alone.

Integer horizontal/vertical pixel repetition, including sprites. 160/320-wide logical modes can repeat to 320/640; 100 lines repeat to 200. Reject 640-wide graphics or 80-column text on a 320-only monitor; software viewport is a separately reported service. Artemis card repeats legacy pixels/lines to 640×400 for Mono Pro; never downscales 400 lines to an old monitor.

Explicit 1-bit and 2-bit pixel-to-output-index maps. Color indices are not brightness values. On grayscale displays map RGB palette entries to luminance; Mono I direct DAC requires host index mapping.
Per-application context state; no accidental shared cursor, selection or editing globals. Aurelia remains single-foreground; Artemis may manage multiple isolated application contexts.
Native Logix-aware editors, forms, spreadsheets, file views and application lifecycle. Legacy CP/M console and Unix-compatible terminal sessions retain explicitly selected compatibility profiles.
Forward-looking alternative-history design at the TUI launch; later DOS, Windows and Linux conventions are design references, not claimed historical 1978 standards.
Arrows navigate; Ctrl modifies navigation granularity; Shift extends selection using the same movement destination.
Ctrl supplies editing/document commands; Alt supplies menu and system actions. System-reserved commands cannot be rebound by applications.
Dispatch stable logical command identifiers separately from physical keys. Resolve focused control, active dialog, application and system ownership explicitly.
Show shortcuts in menus/help; disabled or unavailable commands report their state. Compatibility profiles are explicit, visible and never silently mixed.

chapter_name: Editing behaviour and ownership of state

sources.text: Fixed anchor and moving caret. Plain Left/Right collapses to the corresponding selection edge without an extra step; vertical motion retains the preferred column. Home/End target displayed-line boundaries.

Shared word-boundary implementation groups letters, digits and underscore; freeze punctuation/whitespace traversal in conformance examples. Plain-text paragraphs are separated by blank lines; structured editors use paragraph objects.

Copy/Cut without a selection does nothing. Cut removes data only after clipboard transfer succeeds. Delete preserves clipboard. Typing or pasting replaces a selection as one undoable operation; allocation failure must not partially destroy selected content.
Report Save success only after successful completion; retain modified state on failure. Close offers Save/Discard/Cancel for modified content; Quit checks every modified document.

Spreadsheet navigation selects cells until cell-edit mode, which uses text rules. Editor Tab indents and Shift+Tab unindents; form Tab traverses focus. F6 leaves a multiline editor. Esc acts on only one innermost context per press.
Insertion mode by default. Overwrite is an explicit visibly indicated option; bare Insert does not toggle it by default.
Formatting Ctrl+B/I/U is optional in capable editors. Whole-line deletion, duplication, transpose and rectangular selection remain menu commands outside the common shortcut core.

Aurelia remains single-foreground. Alt+Tab exposes the supported launcher/switch mechanism and does not promise concurrent applications or preserved running state. Query lifecycle capabilities on each host.
Native TUI Ctrl+S/Q are Save/Quit and must not be intercepted by software flow control. Terminal sessions may preserve configured XON/XOFF behavior.
Optional WordStar/Emacs profiles are whole opt-in keymaps, not conflicting default aliases. Legacy CP/M control-character semantics are preserved outside native TUI contexts.
Key identity plus Ctrl/Shift/Alt modifier state; text translation is separate. Preserve Ctrl+Shift navigation and Ctrl+Shift letter distinctions.

Traditional byte terminals can conflate Tab/Ctrl+I, Enter/Ctrl+M, Esc/Ctrl+[, Backspace/Ctrl+H and shifted Ctrl letters. Advertise capabilities and offer menu equivalents rather than ambiguous shortcut promises.
Existing keyboard exact layout, event encoding, rollover and firmware remain engineering gates; required controls are conformance requirements, not a qualified new hardware revision.

Standalone file-based integration remains the baseline: Pulse reads and edits supported closed Abacus documents with exclusive writer ownership. Pulse 3.0 additionally supports embedded scripting in Abacus 3.0 under technology.abacus_embedded_pulse; this does not change Pulse 1.x.
Recompile shared application code with the target compiler and target libraries. Adapt OS-specific modules, resource budgets and assembly; binary compatibility is a separate CP/M-80 module path.
demonstrate to third-party developers that moving from the 8-bit platform to Artemis is comparatively easy
Single foreground versus multiple processes: explicit context ownership and shared-service synchronization.
Use compact software-managed mapping records and a 32-entry translation cache; do not allocate a flat table for the entire 32-bit virtual address space.
No ASIDs in v1. Flush unlocked user translations at each address-space switch; retain wired kernel translations.
One compact record per allocated virtual mapping, indexed by virtual page; stored in kernel-owned RAM. Software resolves misses. No flat 4 GB page table.
128 mapped pages require 1024 bytes of mapping records per process, plus indexing and process metadata. This is an illustrative budget, not a measured total.
Keep trap vectors, refill routine, kernel stack and map-access window permanently translatable; refill must not depend on an unresolved user mapping.
Translation miss traps before a memory side effect; software finds the mapping, fills an entry and retries.
Writes to a copy-on-write mapping cause a protection fault; allocate/copy a page, update mappings and retry.
Unmapped or unauthorized addresses cause a process fault. Allocation failure returns a defined error or terminates the offending process according to the fault contract.
Instruction restart must preserve exact state; multi-register loads/stores need defined restart semantics or restrictions.
DMA uses physical addresses with pinned buffers or bounded bounce buffers; never translate arbitrary user pointers asynchronously.
Harvest referenced/dirty bits before replacing or flushing translation entries; merge them into kernel mapping metadata.
Maintain physical-frame reference counts for shared and copy-on-write pages; invalidate stale writable translations before sharing a frame.
Begin with a conservative registered translation stage and an explicit wait/ready handshake. Do not promise zero wait states.

Evaluate 12 MHz MMU at 6 MHz CPU and 16 MHz MMU at 8 MHz CPU, phase-locked to the CPU clock. A two-phase translation/permission lookup may reduce hit latency only if address setup, comparison and output timing close.
Measure hit/miss latency, context-switch cost, DMA contention and workload hit rate. A faster MMU clock cannot remove DRAM wait time or software refill cost.

sources.text: Independently select both full-width modules and each rank within a capacity bank; 32-bit data bus shared by selected module. Multiplex row/column addresses and refresh every rank.
Shared module edge interface with separate board routing for selected DRAM rails; no chip-footprint interchangeability assumption.
Installed configuration is specified; maximum board capacity/socket count remain open and are not the CPU address-space limit.
Installed configuration is specified; maximum board capacity/socket count remain open and are not the CPU address-space limit.
Two matched 32-bit modules per capacity bank, selected independently on the 32-bit bus. Fill banks in order; all ranks require decoding and refresh. Cross-host connector/timing qualification pending.
Use the shared module catalogue. Install matched pairs; preserve specified capacity. Replace all modules when changing density. Previous 16-bit population recipes are superseded.

chapter_name: ABI, memory protection and portable applications

sources.text: Qualified Z80 binaries execute on the Z80 guest processor, not natively on the new host ISA; OS/memory/peripheral bridging remains required.
Z80 executes the enhanced CP/M environment in its local 64 KB RAM; ERA executes the AIONix host driver. This is neither ERA execution of Z80 instructions nor a C-source port.
A bounded shared mailbox or dual-ported transfer window and interrupt/doorbell signals; reserve its CP/M-side RAM before advertising TPA
CP/M BIOS and Logix TUI/device stubs marshal requests; applications using these interfaces do not access Artemis registers.
A privileged AIONix driver validates guest buffer offsets and lengths, copies data and dispatches console/display, file, printer and clock operations.
Guest-visible drive images preserve CP/M semantics. Host filesystem translation is a separate explicit mode, not transparent raw-volume sharing.
One outstanding synchronous guest request initially; host completes then signals the guest. Add polling fallback and timeout/reset recovery. Never allow a guest to supply an unchecked ERA pointer.
Render an isolated guest text surface through host display services. Capability queries describe that guest surface, not every ERA capability.
Support documented enhanced CP/M/Logix API applications. Arbitrary direct Aurelia hardware access, undocumented mapper use, timing-sensitive code and unvirtualized expansion ROMs are not guaranteed.

chapter_name: Portable networking over a local link

sources.text: IP is kept above the Logix-specific physical/data-link layer so future faster link technologies can preserve higher-level software.
hub-controlled polling/grant; one station is granted transmit access at a time, avoiding collision-detection hardware

Stream the granted frame to other admitted ports at the common rate; destination filtering and CRC validation occur in adapters. No independent per-port rates, frame-store switching or rate conversion in the 1981 baseline.
One common rate across all admitted stations; one transmitter at a time. Port count does not multiply shared bandwidth. Application throughput is lower and remains unvalidated.
The stable logix_lan100_link identifier is retained for references; 100 denotes the mandatory startup/fallback rate, not the maximum rate.
Each listed host requires qualification.
Each listed host requires qualification.
Each listed host requires qualification.
Each listed host requires qualification.

Intersection of adapter hardware capability, firmware-enforced host qualification ceiling and configured cable/reliability limits. Platform ceilings are design qualification targets, not measured throughput claims.
Hub selects the highest rate in the intersection of its own capability and every admitted station/link capability. A 100-only station or link limits the whole network to 100 kbit/s.
Choose the highest common candidate; announce a switch epoch and bounded idle interval at 100 kbit/s and collect acknowledgments from all admitted stations.
Drain the current frame and stop grants before changing the distributed clock. Do not switch with a missing acknowledgment.
Run bounded test frames on every admitted link at the candidate rate; resume normal grants only after every link passes.

On failed qualification or persistent link errors, return to 100 kbit/s for coordination, exclude the failed candidate and try the next lower common rate. If 100 fails, isolate the faulty port and report the fault.

Periodically drain traffic and open an announced 100 kbit/s discovery window. New stations join only after coordinated renegotiation; admitting a slower station lowers the common rate. Discovery windows consume shared bandwidth.

Adapters use a timeout independent of the distributed bit clock. On lost clock/control or switch timeout, stop transmitting and await the hub at 100 kbit/s. The hub watchdog restores 100 kbit/s and a new negotiation epoch; never allow unilateral station transmission at a different rate.

sources.text: Local adapter RAM, additional to host system RAM. Partition transmit/receive buffers and metadata; freeze maximum frame length and IP MTU to fit complete frames before implementation. Physical RAM chip count remains unresolved.

Grant unicast only when the destination advertises credit for a complete frame; reserve that credit until completion. Broadcast requires credit from all intended admitted receivers. Timeouts revoke stale credits; bounded queues and retry/error reporting prevent indefinite blocking. Use flow control first for receiver pressure, not automatic rate changes.

No per-byte interrupt requirement. Aurelia at 250 kbit/s has 128 CPU clocks per raw byte at 4 MHz; Aurelia+ at 500 kbit/s has 96 at 6 MHz. Validate worst-case service latency. A persistently slow host may advertise a lower configured ceiling.
Mixed-platform admission, missing acknowledgments, clock loss, buffer exhaustion and broadcast backpressure
One AION system-controller chip replaces mapper registers and selected decode/control logic; external clock/reset/interrupt and electrical buffers remain as required.
Read-only code and constants execute directly from ROM where practical. Mutable state, stacks and buffers reside in RAM.

CPU uses temporary 4 KiB display-memory windows or auto-incrementing upload ports. DMA uses physical source banks and target-ready video ports. Video controller independently refreshes display DRAM and arbitrates sprite SRAM; sprite storage is not system RAM.
Initialize refresh and boot mapping before RAM use; disable DMA and clear pending ownership on reset. Warm boot aborts/drains DMA before restoring bank maps.
Installed RAM is accessible, but system workspaces and the resident Business Tools workspace reduce application memory.

chapter_name: CP/M application boundary and service dispatch

sources.text: At launch, the little-endian word at 0006H (the operand of JMP at 0005H) points to the BDOS entry stub at the exclusive top of usable contiguous application RAM. Keep the entire advertised range writable RAM.

Reserve 4 KB at the top of lower RAM for the entry stub and resident workspace, in addition to F000–FFFF common system RAM. These are the initial design allocations, not measured image sizes. If implementation requires more workspace, revise the boot profile before application launch and report the actual lower boundary.
Warm boot restores vectors and the normal map. Legacy programs with hardcoded addresses beyond the published boundary remain unsupported.
Disable optional resident tools or choose a smaller TPA when networking needs more RAM; never silently consume advertised program memory.
lx_memory_query returns installed RAM, TPA bounds, reserved bytes and optional banked-handle capacity. Standard CP/M programs need not use it.
Stress CPU/DMA/refresh/peripherals and display together at both host clocks and process/temperature corners.
Validate hidden and expanded RAM refresh, physical DMA bounds, page-crossing segmentation, abort and warm boot.

sources.text: Latch physical source/destination bank and offsets on start. CPU mapping changes cannot redirect an active transfer; split logical buffers at 4 KiB boundaries before programming physical segments. Reject ROM writes, unmapped banks and out-of-range lengths.
Bounded bursts with guaranteed CPU and refresh service; device-ready/WAIT handshake; video uploads yield to video-controller fetch deadlines. Numeric grant limits require cycle-level validation.
Disk/FlexiBUS DMA requires qualified request/ready or FIFO endpoints and drivers; legacy programmed I/O remains supported.
System DRAM only, including hidden banks and expansion. Video controller refreshes display DRAM; sprite SRAM needs no refresh.

Always-running timer, row counter and refresh arbitration during CPU execution, HALT and DMA; initialize before enabling RAM use. Match row count and retention deadlines to each qualified system DRAM type.

This is the normal application mapping. Within it, 7000–EFFF remains switchable in 4 KB pages. A system call can temporarily map ROM or video RAM there, preserving and later restoring any hidden RAM. F000–FFFF remains common system RAM.
The card fills B000–EFFF with RAM in the normal view. ROM, cartridges and video RAM use temporary overlays within 7000–EFFF; the underlying RAM retains its contents.

Shared C function names, argument meanings, ownership rules and error semantics across target-specific implementations.
Optional extensions are obtained through the stable dispatcher or checked extension lookup; never require an unresolved future symbol merely to test availability.

sources.text: Accepted AIONix2 ROM-backed planning baseline. Preserve documented ERA AIONix binaries through versioned compatibility; individual applications and editions require qualification. External application ROM cartridges are not added by the internal system ROM decision.

Accepted AIONix2 ROM-backed planning baseline. Preserve documented ERA AIONix binaries through versioned compatibility; individual applications and editions require qualification. External application ROM cartridges are not added by the internal system ROM decision.
Enumerate usable configurations; optional stable names supplement opaque mode identifiers and descriptive properties. Do not assume every named mode is supported.
Identify monitor through Logix bidirectional Control; use an explicit configured profile on identification failure. Report the intersection of host, monitor and memory-allocation capabilities.
New identifiers may be selected by descriptor properties without changing an older application. Unsupported requests fail cleanly.
Optional later service: preserve a logical canvas and convert to available output. Not guaranteed at launch; report emulation and validate RAM, quality and speed.

Aurelia/Aurelia+ and Artemis 128 economy card: native 40×25 and 80×25 with 8×8 cells. Artemis 256/PRO professional card adds 80×25 at 8×16 and 80×40 at 8×10 with Mono Pro. Intersect card and monitor capabilities.
Text and bitmap modes reuse the same video RAM. Do not reserve all text maps, font storage and a full bitmap simultaneously.

Previous screen pixels are not preserved by default. An explicit preservation request may use a system-RAM buffer only if allocation succeeds; unsupported or unaffordable requests return a defined error before changing the mode.

Aurelia family and Artemis economy card: 16 KiB, two 8000-byte bitmap pages or one 16000-byte page. Artemis professional card: 32 KiB, two 8000/16000-byte pages or one 32000-byte page. All text modes support two pages and one shared font; five sprites use separate SRAM.
Draw glyphs from ROM/system resources into the bitmap; bitmap mode does not require a complete resident character-generator table in video RAM.
Latch page and sprite positions during vertical blank; shared-font and sprite-pattern changes need separate synchronization.
Documented contemporary C subset shared by both compilers; later ANSI C features are not implicitly available.
Publish signedness, alignment, calling conventions and aggregate layout per target before binary ABI freeze.
No CPU floating-point hardware or cross-target floating representation is assumed; numeric libraries specify precision, rounding, overflow and format.
Logic, SRAM, DRAM capacitor/sense circuits and analog require separate qualification. One metal baseline; additional polysilicon is recipe-specific.
Logic, SRAM, DRAM capacitor/sense circuits and analog require separate qualification. One metal baseline; additional polysilicon is recipe-specific.
Logic, SRAM, DRAM capacitor/sense circuits and analog require separate qualification. One metal baseline; additional polysilicon is recipe-specific.
Logic, SRAM, DRAM capacitor/sense circuits and analog require separate qualification. One metal baseline; additional polysilicon is recipe-specific.
Formatted-table tabs coexist with freeform sparse worksheet tabs. Independently implemented historical Abacus format; no dependency on modern Parquet libraries or claim of Parquet compatibility.
Specify rounding, collation, overflow, null/error semantics and checked conversions; preserve leading-zero identifiers as text.
Smallest compression/encoding unit; byte-bounded buffers and dictionaries. Group/page sizes require measurement on target RAM and disks.
Versioned schema, chunk/page locations and supported min/max/null-count statistics. Bound metadata memory and permit incremental access.
Skip only when valid conservative statistics prove no match; handle nulls, sort order and pending edits. Predicate pushdown evaluates filters early and is distinct from statistics-based skipping.
Dictionary, RLE, bit packing and suitable numeric encodings with uncompressed fallback. Compression is dataset-dependent; no guaranteed 75–90% reduction or heavy codec requirement.
Stream and batch scans; bound dictionaries, query state and join memory. Use temporary disk storage or report resource limits; do not require whole tables or row groups resident.

Use a bounded edit buffer/change log with stable row IDs; merge pending changes into reads. Rewrite affected storage on save/compaction, update or invalidate statistics and preserve a consistent visible snapshot.
Validate replacement data and footer before recoverable replacement; retain prior valid version until success. Do not publish incomplete metadata or silently skip corrupt blocks.
Abacus native expressions or documented SQL expression subset with shared type, decimal, null and error rules.
Side-effect-free row expressions; track dependencies and reject cycles. Values computed on demand; persisted statistics require valid materialization.
Scalar lookup requires unique-key relationship; missing keys and duplicate keys have explicit behavior, never arbitrary first-match selection.
One-to-many/many-to-many joins produce derived query tables rather than silently changing scalar column cardinality.

Read-only SELECT projections, WHERE filters, GROUP BY aggregates and equijoins over local formatted tables; document supported syntax and resource limits. No claim of complete SQL standard or general transaction engine.

chapter_name: Launch schema and later nested values

sources.text: Bounded arrays, maps and structs with explicit depth/size limits, expandable presentation, indexing, null and aggregation semantics; implementation milestone not yet dated.
Standalone offline document access remains available; embedded Pulse 3.0 is a separate mode hosted by Abacus 3.0.
Abacus owns the open document and file writer. Scripts use its API; no concurrent independent Pulse writer.
Bounded iteration and operations on cells, tables, formulas, queries and report layouts; reuse Pulse language/runtime semantics.
Explicit script actions may modify documents; ordinary formula/virtual-column evaluation is side-effect-free. Define cancellation, error recovery, grouped undo and recalculation boundaries.
Track changed dependencies, invalidate stale caches and recalculate through the matching Abacus evaluator. Avoid whole-document duplication in RAM.
Preserve standalone version checks, recoverable replacement saves and older edition restrictions. Embedding does not backport 3.0 features to Z80 editions.
Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta 0..255. Byte 1: bits 7..4 palette register 0..15, bits 3..0 red. Byte 2: bits 7..4 green, bits 3..0 blue. Each RGB component is 4 bits.

Offsets count physical active output scanlines, independent of logical mode scaling. Start accumulator at 0 each frame; add delta before applying entry. Delta 0 permits multiple writes before the same line, including line 0. Reject overflow, out-of-frame targets and excess writes per line; never wrap. Bridge gaps above 255 with an explicitly redundant write preserving the current register value.

Prefetch records into dedicated sequencer registers/FIFO, outside the 1536-byte allocation. Execute during blanking before the target active scanline; reset pointer/counter at frame start. Restore a saved 16-register base palette every vertical blank before replay. Line-0 entries follow base restoration.

Single list buffer. CPU writes only with sequencer disabled or after completion before the next frame; arm validated count/base palette at vertical blank. No implicit full-list double buffer; late/incomplete updates remain disabled.

Opt-in capability extension over the existing Control pair, host-to-monitor during the reserved blanking window, clocked from pixel Clock. No simultaneous capability readback. Proposed fixed 32-bit write: 4-bit opcode, 4-bit register, 12-bit RGB, 4 reserved zero bits, CRC-8 (poly 0x07, init 0, no reflection/xorout), MSB first. Reset command framing at blank start; specify setup/hold, turnaround and CRC failure behavior before release.

640x400 raster has 160 blank clocks = about 7.44 us. Target maximum four 32-bit commands per blank (128 clocks, about 5.95 us), leaving 32 clocks for guards/commit/settling. This is a qualification target, not an unconditional measured guarantee. Advertise the validated per-raster limit; 512 total entries does not allow 512 writes on one scanline.

Monitor validates complete commands into staging registers and commits together before active pixels. Reject invalid/late batches, retain previous palette and latch diagnostic status; never update midway through an active line.

For raster effects on Color Pro use the 640x400 physical raster, including line-doubled 640x200. Other raster/monitor combinations require their own advertised timing budget. Old monitors receive only supported vertical-retrace commands.

Palette is global to text, bitmap and sprites at each scanline. 2 bpp still selects only four background indices on a line; 4 bpp selects sixteen. More colours across different lines do not imply a larger per-pixel index or arbitrary 4096-colour bitmap.

Pointing-device class, two buttons, relative X/Y, two independent signed roller axes; versioned capability record. Use negotiated existing FlexiBUS rates, framing, CRC and request/response discipline.

Sequenced bounded report: accumulated signed relative X/Y motion, signed vertical/horizontal roller deltas, current button mask and ordered button transitions. ACK/retry must not duplicate motion or clicks.
Host polls with a bounded service budget; device buffers events. Coalesce motion but preserve button transitions; report overflow and resynchronize button state on reset/removal.

Primary button focuses/selects/activates; secondary opens context actions where provided. Middle-finger roller scrolls vertically; thumb roller scrolls horizontally. Wheels have no implicit press buttons.
Architecture-neutral class driver for Z80 CP/M Platform Extensions and ERA AIONix. Attach while port quiescent; no unsupported hot-plug claim.
Hit-test visible enabled standard controls; primary click focuses fields/selects list items and activates buttons/menu actions.
Text widgets support click-to-place caret and drag selection; scrollbar and roller actions respect widget bounds.
Capture drags to their originating context, release on button-up/cancel/removal, respect modal dialogs and clipping.
Vertical roller scrolls the hovered scrollable control, falling back to the focused control; thumb roller similarly scrolls horizontally.

No application source changes for standard controls managed by the TUI library. Existing binaries gain support only when they call replaceable/system TUI services; statically linked copies require relinking with the updated library. Custom drawing, direct console polling and non-TUI applications require explicit adaptation. No blanket mouse retrofit for all CP/M programs.
Aurelia has one foreground application; AIONix routes events only to the appropriate active/context-owned controls, with modal/capture rules and no input leakage.

Library-managed pointer with bounded save/restore on software-rendered targets or optional sprite rendering; application code need not change. A hardware pointer consumes an existing sprite unless separately provisioned; no sixth sprite is implied.

The 64 KiB card occupies the existing dedicated video slot; the 128 KiB professional card occupies one general 32-bit expansion slot. Independent framebuffers, clocks and palettes; freeze address windows, interrupts, DMA arbitration and power budget before release.

Colour display hosts commands/status; 800x600 monochrome display hosts the CAD canvas. Explicit display handles, coordinate transforms, keyboard/mouse focus and cursor ownership; no implicit shared framebuffer.

Keep vector geometry authoritative. CPU tessellates curves; redraw damaged regions and exposed pan strips. XOR is for temporary simple cursors, not erasing antialiased overlapping geometry. No full-frame 2bpp double buffer in 128 KiB.
At 60 Hz visible framebuffer reads alone average 7.2 MB/s. Qualify banked/wide memory, line buffering, refresh priority and accelerator/host arbitration under worst-case drawing load.
Capability-query extension with software fallback for development on the existing display; later hardware accelerates the same semantics. CAD canvas requires explicit mouse adaptation.

Short in-order interlocked pipeline, ALU result forwarding, explicit load-use stalls, early branch-target calculation and flushing; preserve ERAv1 PC and instruction semantics, with no new visible delay slots.
Documented ERAv1 user binaries retain an execution path. New privileged/MMU features require OS support; no socket, mainboard or unqualified peripheral compatibility implied.
Interface support target only; no external cache included in the Athena base BOM until selected. DMA coherency must be specified.
Prefer software-managed refill initially; concurrent instruction/data translation remains an implementation decision.
Precisely defined restartable faults for demand paging. ERAv1 already has Data Abort and Prefetch Abort; ERA² strengthens the restart contract rather than introducing aborts for the first time.
Measure workload-specific improvement over 8 MHz ERAv1; former 2–3× objective is not a general promise. Report clock, cache, memory and software configuration with results.
Faulting instruction has no changes or documented resumable state; report instruction address, access address/type and cause.
Validate translations/permissions for multi-access instructions before effects, or define explicit continuation state; device accesses must not be blindly replayed.
Post-acceptance external bus errors are distinct from recoverable translation/protection faults; no claim that all external effects are undoable.
Direct-mapped physically tagged cache with 16-byte lines; organization remains subject to layout and traces.
Coordinate four-word prefetch with requested-word-first refill and early restart where feasible; cancel obsolete branch fetches and prioritize demand data.
Qualify 120 ns row access / about 240 ns random cycle; 150 ns fallback with about 270–300 ns random cycle. Geometry alone does not establish timing.

chapter_name: Mode discovery and shared video memory

sources.text: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.
Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 16 KiB display DRAM. The exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM remains available in every mode.
One shared 2048-byte font; glyph edits affect both pages. Independent font buffering is not advertised in this baseline.
Two descriptor banks hold signed 16-bit X/Y, enable and reserved controls. CPU/DMA uses auto-incrementing SRAM upload ports.
Switch descriptor bank atomically at vertical blank. Pattern writes require scheduled access or disabling affected sprites; 1 KiB does not hold two complete pattern sets.
Five sprites in every text/bitmap mode, including double-buffered backgrounds. Sprite SRAM never consumes display DRAM.
Two descriptor banks hold signed 16-bit X/Y, enable and reserved controls. CPU/DMA uses auto-incrementing SRAM upload ports.
Switch descriptor bank atomically at vertical blank. Pattern writes require scheduled access or disabling affected sprites; 1 KiB does not hold two complete pattern sets.
Five sprites in every text/bitmap mode, including double-buffered backgrounds. Sprite SRAM never consumes display DRAM.
80 bytes of live two-bank descriptors within a 128-byte reserved area; 48 bytes padding. 640 pattern + 128 descriptor + 256 scratch bytes = 1024.
Trace each wafer to material batch, tool, operator, recipe revision and electrical results; map defects and distinguish random from systematic failures.
Monitor particles, film thickness, sheet resistance, transistor thresholds, contacts and tool drift; use control charts and documented corrective action.
Separate engineering lots from released production; qualify maintenance and tool substitutions before customer manufacture.
Report wafer completion, electrical die yield, accepted speed/retention bins, package yield and good saleable chips per wafer separately.
Qualify ROM image verification and SRAM read/write margins separately from DRAM retention, sensing, refresh and disturb behaviour.
Test across specified voltage and temperature limits; retain lot histories, wafer maps and failure-analysis evidence.
For repairable DRAM revisions, map defects, programme only supported redundancy and retest the complete device; unrepairable launch revisions receive no assumed repair benefit.
